status: Closed — sealed transaction regression and repair verified 2026-09-05; no open follow-up
area: Git governance / sealed commit bundle deletion attribution
finding: TASK-GIT-0029 sealed commit attribution protects add/modify content, but staged deletions are not represented in the sealed bundle because `ls-files -s` has no entry for a staged deletion. An in-scope deleted file can therefore survive in the committed tree instead of being delivered as an intentional deletion.
expectedBehavior: Sealed commit bundles must represent deletion as an explicit tombstone and compare the committed tree against that tombstone. Commit assembly must remove tombstoned paths from the candidate index without re-adding worktree content, and any missing, extra, or wrong-blob result must fail closed before ref mutation.
evidenceOrRepro: Historical reproduction: TASK-GIT-0029 omitted staged deletion tombstones. Current 2026-09-02 reproduction also found a related new-entry substitution: after sealing `src/admitted.txt`, a concurrent worktree/index replacement could be reintroduced by the stat-cache `git add -f` workaround. `commit-attribution-sealed-transaction.test.ts` was red with ATM_COMMIT_ATTRIBUTION_MISMATCH before the repair. Candidate assembly now immediately rewrites every newly-added path to its sealed mode/blob after stat-cache population; the focused regression is green and covers tombstones, blob swaps, extra candidate entries, post-commit tree proof, and live-index reconciliation.
followUp: Fixed. Maintain the sealed-transaction regression; reopening requires a new candidate-tree mismatch that bypasses its pre-ref assertion.
